_comment: sim/open-loop-ac as a `klt sim` request (issue #85): the AC half of the bench.
Circuit: tb_openloop_ac.body.spice -- the same test circuit as ../testbench/tb_openloop_ac.spice.tmpl.
Grid: cornerMOSlv.lib mos_tt/ss/ff/sf/fs [DR-1] x {-40, 27, 125} C x VDD {1.08, 1.20, 1.32} V = 45 corners.
vinp sweeps WITH vdd by index (klt's supply_v semantics), so Vcm = VDD/2 at every corner, as in the harness.
Each process corner is a bundle carrying the template's fixed cornerCAP.lib cap_typ section (the Miller cap is a cap_cmim MIM device).
limits are the RATIFIED bounds of spec/target-spec.md section 2 [DR-2], unrounded: Av0 >= 37.8 dB, GBW >= 4.74 MHz, PM >= 60 deg.
PM is graded through its defining quantity: this bench defines PM = 180 deg + phase(v(out)) at the 0 dB crossing (README 'Sign convention').
vp(out) is the WRAPPED phase, in (-pi, pi]; the harness's PM uses the continuous phase (cph). min -2*pi/3 alone is NOT PM >= 60 deg:
an unstable corner with PM -10 deg reads +170 deg and would pass. max 0 makes the tool verdict fail safe: phase at the UGF is negative
for this non-inverting bench, so a positive reading can only be a wrap. With both bounds, the verdict equals PM >= 60 deg for
PM in (-180, 180] deg (continuous phase at the UGF in (-360, 0] deg; more than 360 deg of lag at the UGF is implausible for this two-stage bench).
Residual edge case: near PM ~ 0 deg the bracketing sweep points can straddle the wrap and .meas can interpolate to an arbitrary value
in between (including inside [-2*pi/3, 0]); compare.py's 0.1 deg PM tolerance against the harness's continuous-phase PM catches that.
margin x 180/pi is PM - 60 deg while PM <= 120 deg (above that the max 0 bound is the nearer one). A `.meas` result is not
visible to an `expr` in ngspice's control block (checked on ngspice-42), so the tool cannot add the 180 deg offset itself.
Iq and the per-point DC operating-point sanity checks live in openloop_op.request.json: klt sim runs one analysis per corner
(docs/cli/sim.md 'Still one analysis per corner'); compare.py joins the two envelopes on (process, temperature, vdd). See README.md.
gbw_hz is ngspice's own .meas WHEN interpolation (linear in frequency between the bracketing sweep points); the harness interpolates
in log10(frequency). The bias is one-signed and bounded; compare.py quantifies it -- see README.md 'Measurement method'.
Solver tolerance: ngspice default, no .options reltol/abstol/vntol (DR-0005).
ngspice_init raises the printed digits only (measureprec for .meas, numdgt for expr); it changes no solver setting.
keep_artifacts is false so the committed envelope carries no host-absolute artifact paths; to debug a corner, run a copy of this request with it set (and --outdir outside the repo).

measurements.name: phase_at_ugf_rad
measurements.spice: .meas ac phase_at_ugf_rad find vp(out) when vdb(out)=0
